title: Forge driver refusal v1 (an additive extension of forge-driver/v1)
description: Decision 0103 ruling 1(a) and ruling 4(a): the optional, absent-by-default additions a forge-driver/v1 driver may send. A `result` may carry one typed `refusal` object — the closed class, the provider and route the driver already resolved, the provider's bounded evidence, and an optional HTTP status and retry-after. A `capabilities` message and a `start` may each carry `probe: true`: the driver runs a one-turn probe, and the engine asks for one. The protocol word stays forge-driver/v1 and the message family gains optional fields an old reader ignores; `probe` is never a `supports` entry, whose list the frozen v1 schema closes to resume, checkpoint and cancel. An unresolved route is the explicit null, never a missing key. A present object that cannot be read refuses by name, never as absent.

refusal.description: Present on `result` only, and at most once per invocation. Absent means the driver classified no typed refusal and the engine keeps its untyped path.

probe.description: Present on `capabilities` as the driver's advertisement that it can run a one-turn probe, and on `start` as the engine's request that this invocation is one. Never written as false: an absent field is the only absence.

class.description: The closed machine class. `rate_limit` is the provider's pre-session rate limit; every other refusal is `other` and parks rather than waiting.

provider.description: The provider name the adapter's declaration uses (claude, lanetally, codex, dsh, exec, ...), filled from the adapter and never parsed from prose.

route.description: The route the driver serves the pinned model on: the concrete model id's prefix before its first `/` (decision 0036 ruling 2), from the one predicate the producer and this pattern share (`brokkr-protocol`'s adapters/served_route.rs::route_form). Null is a typed absence: the route could not be resolved, and the engine parks naming it rather than recording a provider-wide cool-down.

words.description: The provider's bounded evidence line: its machine token when it gave one, the HTTP status when it gave that, and a short excerpt of its prose when it gave that. One line, clamped, never a transcript.

status.description: The HTTP status the provider's refusal carried, when it carried one.

retry_after_seconds.description: The provider's own retry-after in whole seconds, when measured. Zero, a negative and a fraction are refused, never read as no retry-after.
